events.title: LIONS, COYOTES & BOBCATS, OH MY!  & one more… GRAY FOX!
events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: Linda Hawley's Nature Adventures! Ages 4-10 with an adult San Diego’s top predators & largest mammals: How do they differ? What do they eat? Where are their habitats? How do we co-exist with them? How do we help them? How do they help us? ABOUT THE PRESENTER: Linda Hawley, Ed.M., delights children & adults alike with the animated enthusiasm she brings to her monthly programs by entertaining them with her PowerPoint presentation, songs, puppets, real animal pelts & nests, replicated skulls, specimens, scats & tracks; take-home craft materials &/or handouts will be provided. EVERYONE HAS FUN LEARNING! Ms. Hawley has 40+ years of experience as a classroom teacher, college professor, naturalist guide & educator for Audubon Society’s OutdoorExplore! & at Mission Trails Regional Park, where she created & taught her “wildly popular” nature classes for 10 years. She is author of NATURE ADVENTURES! A Guidebook of Nature Facts, Songs and Hikes in San Diego County, Sunbelt Publications, Inc. 2017 Her classes go full STEAM ahead: S—Sciences—zoology, biology, botany T—Technology—PowerPoint, Smartphone, computers E—English language, new vocabulary, scientific terms A—Arts, crafts, creativity M—Music—Singing about the fauna of San Diego
events.location: Grant Park, 2310 Camino Del Rio N., San Diego, CA

events.title: San Diego River Gorge Overlook Hike
events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: In celebration of CA Biodiversity week, Please join San Diego River Park Foundation Preserve Steward Bill Martin for this 6 mile out and back hike. This hike follows portions of the old U.S. mail route through the scenic Oak Woodlands and Chaparral where views open to the stunning San Diego River Gorge and Mildred Falls Overlook. events.title: Nature Nights: Bat Walk and Moths 9/12/26
events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: REGISTRATION FOR THIS EVENT IS CLOSED. Join us for a fun evening adventure to learn about the San Diego watershed’s many bat species and their habitats with Dan Taylor. A bat researcher and scientist with Bat Conservation International Dan has more than 30 years of experience working on a wide range of wildlife and conservation issues in the U.S., Central America, and Africa. Dan has been with Bat Conservation Iternational for over 23 years and currently specializes in habitat protection and restoration. After our presentation we will stroll along the river, eavesdropping on the bats we see using our bioacoustics to identify them based on their calls. As the night concludes we will view the moths that have been attracted to our UV light station for up-close observation with Hector Valtierra. An avid moth enthusiast, when Hector isn't out looking for moths and other insects, he works as a microbiology and general biology professor at San Diego community colleges. He is also an avid iNaturalist user and wildlife photographer. All ages are welcome! Be sure to sign up early—space is limited, and our Nature Nights events fill up quickly. Please bring a flashlight or headlamp, a camp chair for the mothing portion, and wear long pants and closed-toe shoes. Consider donating to support our bat conservation program! Follow this link to learn more—every bit of support helps us protect more bats !
events.location: Grant Park, 2310 Camino Del Rio N., San Diego, CA

events.title: Bird Walk at Grant Park
events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: Embark on a fun-filled walk with bird experts Cindy Pencek and Ian Swirka to observe and count the amazing biodiversity of birds that call this section of the river home! You'll not only experience the joy and relaxation of connecting with nature, but will also contribute to conservation efforts through reporting observations on iNaturalist! You’ll also have the opportunity to explore our River Studio at Grant Park—our exciting new nature education center and eco-park featuring beautiful native plant gardens, serving over 5,000 students each year and empowering the next generation of environmental stewards. We hope you can join us! Kids are welcome, with adult supervision. Parking: Please park in the Grant Park parking lot. Access is via the intersection with the stoplight across from iFly Indoor Skydiving. COMPLETE OUR DIGITAL WAIVER OF LIABILITY ( REQUIRED )

events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: Join San Diego Bird Alliance and Jessica Ullyott, founder of Nature Needs SD and local trail guide for a deeper dive into ecosystems. Learn how plants, animals and other factors work together to form the perfect balance by playing the games: Ecologies and Wingspan! Never played these games before? No problem! No experience needed as we all learn and play together. Note: players should be ages 8+ to enjoy this game. If you want to connect with nature all morning, join us for our Bird Walk from 8:00 to 9:30 preceding the game time event led by Bird Expert Cindy Pencek. Learn about the amazing biodiversity of birds found in the watershed and immerse yourself in the beautiful native plant gardens at Grant Park!

events.title: Family Field Trip Community Event, TRACKING & FIELD
events.partner_name: The San Diego River Park Foundation
events.description: Introducing Natural LAW Field Trips for the Whole Family! Land • Air • Water – Your Family’s Adventure Starts Here! REGISTRATION AND INFORMATION: https://sandiegoriver.galaxydigital.com/need/detail/?need_id=1178009 For years, parents and chaperones have joined us on student field trips and shared one consistent wish: “I wish they offered these field trips for adults too!” So, we listened. The San Diego River Park Foundation is thrilled to invite families of all ages to experience our immersive Natural LAW Education Program—a series of hands-on learning adventures designed to deepen your connection to the San Diego River, its rich ecology, and its cultural significance. These field trips are FREE, fun, and crafted to create meaningful outdoor memories together while inspiring the next generation of environmental stewards. Explore the Natural LAW Programs Each themed field trip uncovers a different dimension of the natural world. Families rotate through interactive stations, discovering the hidden stories, adaptations, and science that bring our local ecosystems to life. Upcoming Family Field Trip: Location: 2310 Camino Del Rio North, San Diego, CA 92108 Date: Saturday, October 10, 2026 Arrive: 9:45 am Program Start: 10:00am Program End: 12:00pm LAND: Tracking and Field at Grant Park Assume the role of a keen detective investigating the rich tapestry of wildlife and plant life that thrive along the river. Delve deep into the intricate relationships that sustain this vibrant ecosystem. Learn to identify animals by the signs they leave behind Discover an animal’s feeding habits by examining their teeth Uncover the Predator-Prey dynamics and relationship Reveal the natural checks and balances regulating the wild Sharpen your observational skills and witness firsthand how organisms interact, mutually influence one another, and collectively contribute to the harmony and resilience of the riparian ecosystem. Punctuality: Please arrive a few minutes before the event. Groups arriving late will not be able to experience the entire program. Responsibility: Please be aware of your surroundings, as the safety and discipline of children are your primary responsibility. Promote listening, foster excitement, focus, curiosity, and engagement. Encourage observation rather than providing direct answers. Please step away to take phone calls to deter distraction. Environmental Safety: For safety, please remain vigilant, attentive, and engaged. Natural terrain may present unique challenges. We will reasonably accommodate special needs with the understanding that some of the wilderness terrain may pose challenges. Dress for Outdoor Success: Closed-toe shoes and long pants Comfortable clothes that can get wet, dirty, or muddy. Jacket and/or rain jacket (if needed). Sunscreen, bug spray, and a hat. - Bring a filled reusable water bottle. Leave No Trace: Please respect the park and program areas. Ensure you leave these spaces cleaner than you found them, and dispose of all trash properly. Lunch: A shaded picnic area may be available. Please note that the San Diego River Foundation does not provide lunch or supervision during lunch. Please practice Leave No Trace principles at the San Diego River Park and at all outdoor locations.
events.location: Grant Park, 2310 Camino Del Rio N., San Diego, CA
